lead: El Paso plumbing deals with hard water, desert heat, rare hard freezes and slab homes. PipeMend sends licensed local plumbers across El Paso.
risk: hard water scale, slab leaks and burst pipes in hard freezes
risk_short: hard water, slab leaks and frozen pipes
why: Sunset Heights, Kern Place and Central El Paso have homes from the 1900s to the 1950s with galvanized supply lines and cast-iron drains. Most newer homes on the Westside and Eastside sit on slabs.
Hard freezes, like February 2021, burst pipes that run through attics and exterior walls. Many homes use evaporative coolers with their own water lines.
water: El Paso Water blends Rio Grande water with groundwater and runs one of the world's largest inland desalination plants. The water is hard.
tips: Drain your cooler line before the first freeze.
Watch your water bill for slab leak signs.
areas: PipeMend works in Sunset Heights, Kern Place, the Westside, the Upper Valley, the Northeast, the Eastside, Mission Valley and every other neighborhood.
permits: Plumbing permits come from the City of El Paso Planning and Inspections Department, and plumbers must hold a Texas license.

faq.q: Where does El Paso's water come from?
faq.a: El Paso Water uses Rio Grande water in wetter months and groundwater year-round, including brackish water treated at its desalination plant. The blend is hard.
